chunks: My father narrated to me (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah Al-Jamurani, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: Crying and grief (jaz') are disliked for the servant in any matter he grieves over, except crying and grief over Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). Verily, in that, he is rewarded.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on crying and showing grief over Imam Husayn compared to other matters?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a unique theological exception where the general dislike of excessive emotional display (jaz') is reversed into a meritorious act specifically for mourning Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). It highlights the distinct Shia emphasis on transforming grief into a spiritual practice that earns divine reward, distinguishing it from worldly sorrow.
